purpose: Which difference peaks appear against more than one independent reference. Rubin is the only term the pairings share, so a repeated peak is on the Rubin side and a solitary one belongs to the reference that shows it.
matchedOnSky: Positions are matched in sky coordinates, not pixels: the pairings sit on 0.4, 0.263 and 0.25 arcsec grids, so the same pixel offset is a different angle in each.
onSourceExcluded: Only off-source peaks are cross-matched. A peak on a bright source is a PSF-match residual that appears in every pairing by construction, so confirming one would mean nothing.
caveat: Confirmation across references is not a detection. The filter colour term is now measured and small -- -0.080 mag per mag against DECam, +0.007 against PS1, linear to under 4 millimagnitudes -- so a shared colour effect is a weaker explanation than it was, but the pairings still share the aperture method and the Rubin frame itself. What this test removes is the larger population of per-reference artefacts.
